standard_prerequisites.name: Extending a coherent sheaf from an open neighbourhood of a point
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Cohomology of Schemes, label coherent-lemma-extend-coherent, invoked at proof line 3867
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the ideal sheaf I_{i,p} inside O_{Z_i} mapping isomorphically onto F^p/F^{p+1} near the generic point xi_i.

core_obligations: Make the first map well defined because the two direct sums of structure sheaves are coherent by local finiteness, and the second map well defined by the additive-function criterion applied to the additive function F -> [F]_k which kills Coh_{<=k-1}(X); the composite first-then-second is the identity by inspection (proof lines 3782-3795).

For the other composite, replace F by F/F' with F' the kernel of F -> direct sum of the generic stalks, so the remaining support has dimension at most k-1 and the class in K_0 is unchanged; this reduces to F' = 0 (proof lines 3798-3818).

Filter each generic stalk with one-dimensional successive quotients, form the coherent subsheaves F^p cut out by kernels into the direct sum of stalks, use the two short exact sequences of direct sums to write [F] as the class of the direct sum of the graded pieces, replace each graded piece by an ideal sheaf I_{i,p} in O_{Z_i}, and compare the resulting quotients Q and Q' which both lie in Coh_{<=k-1}(X) (proof lines 3821-3894).
proof_roadmap: Well-definedness of both maps and the easy composite: local finiteness for the direct sums, additivity of the cycle class, and the additive-function criterion (proof lines 3782-3795).
Reduction step: kill the part of F supported in dimension at most k-1 by cutting out the generic stalks, which is invisible in the quotient category K_0 (proof lines 3798-3818).

Graded reduction: filtrations of the generic stalks give the subsheaves F^p, two exact sequences of direct sums identify [F] with the class of the graded pieces, and an ideal-sheaf replacement plus the comparison of Q and Q' identifies that class with the class of the direct sum of O_{Z_i}^{n_i} (proof lines 3821-3894).
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the group of k-cycles of a scheme locally of finite type over S with K_0 of the quotient of the coherent sheaves of dimension at most k by those of dimension at most k-1 through two explicit maps (statement lines 3756-3779, tag 02S9). One direction is a formal additive-function argument, but the other needs real work: the proof reduces an arbitrary coherent F by cutting out the part supported in dimension at most k-1, filters the stalks at the generic points of the components of [F]_k, glues the resulting kernels back into coherent subsheaves, and then replaces each graded piece by an ideal sheaf inside O_{Z_i} so that two comparison quotients land in Coh_{<=k-1}(X). This multi-step gluing goes well beyond a routine citation, so the claim is H2.
